content: Calcium Channel Blockers: Nifedipine: Administered as 20 mg orally in three trial arms. Administered as 20 mg orally combined with 10 mg sublingually in one trial arm. Administered as either 10 mg or 20 mg orally in one trial arm. Administered as 5 mg sublingually in one trial arm. Administered as 10 mg orally in five trial arms. Administered as 10 mg with the route unspecified in one trial arm. Administered as 10 mg sublingually in eight trial arms. Administered as 20 mg orally combined with 10 mg sublingually in one trial arm. Administered as 20 mg orally in eight trial arms. Administered as 30 mg orally in ten trial arms. Administered as 30 mg sublingually in one trial arm. Administered as 10–40 mg sublingually in one trial arm. Nicardipine: Administered as 2 mg/min intravenously in one trial arm. Administered as 3 mg/hour intravenously in one trial arm. Administered as 40 mg orally in one trial arm. Magnesium Sulfate: Administered as 4 g intravenously in three trial arms. Administered as 6 g intravenously in one trial arm. Administered as 7.5 mg intravenously in eleven trial arms. Administered as 300 µg/min intravenously in one trial arm. Nitric Oxide Donors: Glyceryl Trinitrate: Administered transdermally in two trial arms. Isosorbide Dinitrate: Administered sublingually in one trial arm. Maternal Outcomes: Serious adverse effects were reported in varying proportions across different interventions, with some outcomes not estimable. Treatment cessation due to side effects was likely increased in some cases, uncertain in others, and showed no significant difference in certain interventions. Specific side effects such as palpitations, headache, nausea/vomiting, tachycardia, cardiac arrhythmias, hypotension, pulmonary edema, dyspnea, and maternal infection were variably reported, with outcomes ranging from probable increases, possible increases, no difference, or uncertainty depending on the intervention. Fetal and Neonatal Outcomes: Perinatal death, fetal death, and neonatal death before 28 days showed no significant differences in most cases, with some outcomes uncertain or not estimable. Respiratory morbidity was likely unaffected or possibly reduced in some cases. Neurodevelopmental morbidity and gastrointestinal morbidity outcomes were uncertain or showed no significant differences in most cases. Neonatal infection outcomes were generally unaffected or uncertain. Mean birth weight and the proportion of infants with birth weight <2000 g or <2500 g showed no significant differences or possible reductions in some cases.
